φάγρος.definition: sea-bream or braize, Pagrus vulgaris; Cret., whetstone, Simm.27

φαζάλη.definition: a disease contracted in the Red Sea, Id

φαῖνοψ.definition: bright-eyed, conspicuous, Hymn.Is. 31, cf. Man.4.239: in Il. only as pr.n

φάκινος.definition: made of lentils, Sopat.1; i.e. of the consistency of Zos.Alch.p.172 B

φάκιον.definition: decoction of lentils, used as an emetic, Hp.Morb.2.43

φακός.definition: duckweed, Lemna minor, Dsc.1.12, 4.87; anything shaped like lentils

φαλάγγιον.definition: a kind of venomous spider; spider-wort, Lloydia graeca, a herb, said to cure this spider's bite, Dsc.3.108

φάλαρον.definition: boss or disc, mostly in; bandages for the cheek, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.44, Sor.Fasc.18

φαλκίδιον.definition: the minimum share of an estate which must be left to the heirs under the Lex Falcidia, PMasp.97v71 , al

φαναῖος.definition: giving or bringing light, of Zeus, E.Rh.355 ; of Apollo, in Chios, Achae.35

φάνσις.definition: = II.1, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.4; morning twilight, Gloss

φάραγξ.definition: cleft, chasm, esp. in a mountain; metaph., of the anus, Sotad.2.2

φάρσος.definition: any piece cut off or severed, portion; = velamen, Gloss.; = vexillum, ibid.; protective sheets or coverings, J.AJ3.8.2; ib.3.6.4; ibid

φάρυγξ.definition: less freq. , also; dewlap of a bull. Hld.2.1

φασκάς.definition: a kind of duck, Alex.Mynd. ap. Ath.9.395d, cf

φαττάγης.definition: perh. pangolin or scaly ant-eater, manis, Ael.NA16.6

φαῦσις.definition: lighting, illumination; Astron. = heliacal rising, Theo Sm.p.137 H

φαυστήρ.definition: lamp or candelabrum, or perh. large window, IG42.109 ii105.147

φάψ.definition: gen. wild pigeon, A.Frr.210, 257, Arist.HA593a15, al., Lyc.580

φέκλη.definition: = Lat. faecula, Ruf.Fr.115, Crito ap.Gal.12.490; cf

φελλόδρυς.definition: holm-oak, Quercus Ilex var. agrifolia, Thphr.HP1.9.3, 3.3.3, 3.16.3

φέρμα.definition: that which is borne, fruit of; fruit of the earth, Id.Supp.690

φηγός.definition: Dor. Theoc.9.20, = Valonia; acorn of the same tree, Ar.Pax1137 , Pl.R.372c, Theoc. l.c., D.Chr.6.62

φῆμις.definition: poet. for speech, talk, Il.10.207; common opinion or judgement expressed in talk, 14.239, cf. 16.75; their 'bitter gossip', 6.273; . . Ibyc.9

φήνη.definition: a kind of vulture, perh. lammergeyer, Gypaëtus barbatus, Od.16.217, cf. 3.372, Ar.Av.304, Arist.HA592b5, 619b23, cf. sacred to Athena, Ael.NA12.4

φήρ.definition: gen. Aeol. for pl. Simon.59 ; of the Centaurs, Il.1.268, 2.743; in sg., Pi.P.3.4, 4.119:—in Ion. writers of Satyrs , Gal.17.38; of Marsyas, Telest.1.5

φθίσις.definition: —wasting away, perishing; of the moon, waning, Arist.HA582b2, GA767a4

φθόνος.definition: ill-will or malice, esp. envy or jealousy of; a cause for indignation, a reproach, E.Hec.288

φιλαίτιος.definition: fond of bringing accusations, fault-; liable to censure, D.10.70

φιλάνωρ.definition: Dor. for fond of a; kindly, B.1.40; fond of men, of dolphins, Pi.Fr.236

φιλέξοδος.definition: fond of going out or gadding about, Axiop.4.4 codd. Stob

φίληβος.definition: loving youth: only as pr. n. Philebus

φιλίστωρ.definition: fond of learning, Vett.Val.17.24; title of work by Hierocl., Tz.H.7.716; without St.Byz. s. vv. et

φιλόσοφος.definition: lover of wisdom; Pythagoras called; philosopher, i. e. one who speculates on truth and reality, defined as Pl.R.475e; of Aristotle, Plu.2.115b; of Euripides, Ath.13.561a; as the butt of Com., Philem.71.1, Bato5.11, An…

φιλύκη.definition: a shrub, evergreen, privet, Rhamnus Alaternus, Thphr.HP1.9.3, 3.3.1, al

φίλωσις.definition: older form of Iamb.in; Pythag. name for six, ib.37

φιμάριον.definition: Dim. of mask, only in Lat. form fimarium, Gloss

φιτρός.definition: block of wood, log; firebrand, B.5.142, Lyc.913

φίτυμα.definition: shoot, scion, of a son, A.Ag.1281; said a Spartan mother of a cowardly son, Plu.2.241a, cf. Epigr. ibid

φλαῦρος.definition: mostly of things, petty, paltry, trivial, Sol., Pi. ll. cc.; having come to a trivial ending, Hdt.1.120

φλέβιον.definition: Dim. of any one of the smaller; of veins in the earth, Str.8.6.21

φλεγύας.definition: perh. fiery red, red-brown, epithet of the eagle Hes.Sc.134

φλέδων.definition: idle talker, babbler, Timo28; idle talk, Anon. ap.Gal.16.733 , Plu.2.420c

φλέξις.definition: an unknown bird, Ar.Av.884; ardor, flammatus, Gloss

φλοιός.definition: bark of trees, esp. smooth bark (such; husk or skin of certain fruits, Plu.2.684a, Aët.12.1
